principles.title: Specific beats endless.
principles.body: One relevant person, with a reason to meet, never a public list to work through.

principles.title: Both sides choose.
principles.body: A proposed pairing moves forward only after two private yeses. Passing stays private too.

principles.title: Private, always.
principles.body: Names, contact details, and the exact meeting point unlock only when both sides accept.

about.scopeNote: For founders, investors, potential co-founders, and startups with a concrete reason to meet. Not for dating, job seeking, expo-hall pitching, or general networking.

process.heading: From “tell me your side” to “here’s when you’re meeting.”
process.body: Lane is a human operator, not a matching engine, feed, or booking marketplace. The process stays the same; the two sides change.

items.question: Is Lane only for founders looking for investors?
items.answer: No. The service is deliberately two-sided: investors use Lane to find founders, founders use Lane to find investors, potential co-founders find each other, and startups find another startup with a plausible customer or collaboration fit.

items.question: Is Lane a matching app?
items.answer: No. A human operator reads the intake and proposes one pairing at a time. There is no public deck, swipe feed, attendee directory, or automated matching engine.

items.question: Will everyone see my details?
items.answer: No. Intake stays private. Each proposed introduction is shown only to the two relevant sides, and direct contact details stay hidden until both accept.

items.question: What if I pass on a proposed pairing?
items.answer: Lane records the pass privately and moves on. The other side is not given your contact details, and there is no public rejection or ranking.

items.question: What happens after both sides accept?
items.answer: Lane confirms a time and a table or quiet corner. You receive two names and the exact location only after both yeses are in.

items.question: How does the meeting guarantee work?
items.answer: The guarantee applies to the track selected at signup: three accepted meetings on the current event calendar, or the founder-side fee is refunded. Lane books the meeting, not the round, co-founder, customer, or deal.

roiCalculator.heading: ROI Calculator
roiCalculator.subheading: Start with capacity. Then decide what it could be worth.
roiCalculator.disclaimer: A scenario built from your assumptions, not observed results or guaranteed savings. Returned hours are capacity, not an automatic payroll reduction.

copy.workloadIntro: Model introduction research and coordination—not investment proceeds or successful fundraising.
copy.costIntro: Include the costs needed to run this workload. These are your estimates, not a Gabriel quote.
copy.valueIntro: What will you do with the returned hours? Select only outcomes you expect to realize.
copy.reviewNote: Existing-team review uses returned capacity. Additional paid review is included in operating cost, not deducted again from team capacity.
copy.budgetNote: The budget must include models/media, tools, infrastructure, Gabriel fees, and any additional paid review. Do not include unchanged payroll as new spending.
copy.itemizedNote: Enter zero for a cost that does not apply. Additional paid review is calculated from review hours and its actual rate.
copy.annualNote: The same monthly assumptions, without growth or compounding. Hiring savings last only for the entered period.
copy.methodBody: Operating burden removed (negative productivity) returns capacity. Higher-value work (potential positive productivity) creates economic value only if that capacity is used. Hours alone are not cash savings.
copy.formulaLabel: Economic value ÷ operating cost = economic return multiple. Net benefit subtracts operating cost once.
copy.allocationNote: Each hour can be allocated once. Unallocated hours remain capacity, with no euro value.
copy.overlapLabel: These benefits are distinct; I have excluded costs and losses already counted elsewhere.
copy.overlapNote: Error and risk estimates exclude labor savings and the same incident must not appear in both categories. Contribution excludes AI costs, which are deducted separately.
copy.hiringLabel: This hire was genuinely planned and the allocated capacity can cover the work.
copy.reviewedLabel: I have reviewed my outcomes; unselected outcomes have no financial value in this estimate.
copy.throughputResult: Additional work supported by capacity and demand
copy.assumptionsIncomplete: Complete the selected assumptions to calculate financial value.
copy.allocationError: Allocated hours exceed the net capacity available. Reduce the allocations.
copy.reviewError: Review takes more time than the work reduced. No positive capacity is available at these assumptions.
copy.cashError: Avoided spending cannot exceed current spending or have positive value with no hours allocated.
copy.hiringError: Allocated capacity must cover the planned hire hours. Confirm the planned hire and its duration.
copy.riskError: The after probability cannot exceed the before probability for a loss-reduction estimate.
copy.overlapError: Confirm the benefits do not overlap before including them in the financial result.
copy.boundsError: Use values within the displayed limits.
copy.noCurrencyChange: Language changes formatting, not your currency or assumptions.

volume.label: Introduction briefs each month
volume.help: Use a typical month, not a best-case peak.

minutes.label: Hands-on minutes per unit today
minutes.help: Active work time, excluding waiting and elapsed calendar time.

automation.label: Share of that work reduced
automation.help: An illustrative assumption to validate in a pilot, not a performance promise.

review.label: Review minutes per unit
review.help: Human checking still needed after automation.

budget.label: Estimated monthly operating budget
budget.help: Include all models/media, tools, infrastructure, Gabriel fees and additional paid review.

model_cost.label: Models and media generation
model_cost.help: Your monthly estimate, including images or video where applicable.

tools_cost.label: Tools and integrations
tools_cost.help: Browser sessions, connectors and other metered services.

infrastructure_cost.label: Infrastructure
infrastructure_cost.help: Incremental hosting, storage and compute for this workload.

platform_cost.label: Gabriel fees
platform_cost.help: Use your agreed fee or your own budget assumption; this is not a price quote.

review_rate.label: Additional paid review per hour
review_rate.help: Actual extra reviewer spending, not the salary of an unchanged employee.

cash_hours.label: Hours that remove paid work
cash_hours.help: Allocate only work whose overtime, contractor or processing spend will actually stop.

cash_baseline.label: Current monthly spending on that work
cash_baseline.help: The cash budget from which the reduction will come.

cash_avoided.label: Monthly spending you would stop
cash_avoided.help: One explicit amount, not hours multiplied by salary; exclude any planned-hire saving entered separately.

higher_value_hours.label: Hours used for higher-value work
higher_value_hours.help: Hours you can realistically redirect, not the entire capacity by default.

contribution_rate.label: Incremental contribution per hour
contribution_rate.help: Revenue less incremental delivery costs, excluding AI costs counted separately. Not salary or gross revenue.

throughput_hours.label: Hours used for additional volume
throughput_hours.help: This allocation cannot also be used for advisory work or spending reductions.

extra_minutes.label: Team minutes per additional unit
extra_minutes.help: The remaining human effort, including review, needed to deliver one more unit.

demand.label: Additional units with expected demand
demand.help: Capacity alone is not demand. Enter the extra monthly work you expect to take on.

unit_margin.label: Contribution per additional unit
unit_margin.help: Incremental revenue less delivery costs; AI operating costs are deducted separately.

hiring_hours.label: Hours covering the planned hire
hiring_hours.help: Allocate capacity to specific planned work, not a generic full-time-equivalent estimate.

planned_hours.label: Monthly hours the planned hire would cover
planned_hours.help: The allocated capacity must cover this entire workload.

hire_cost.label: Monthly hire cost actually deferred
hire_cost.help: Use the cost of a genuinely planned hire, not the salary of someone already employed.

hire_months.label: Months that hire is deferred
hire_months.help: One to twelve months; the annual estimate stops counting savings after this period.

incidents.label: Expected avoided errors per month
incidents.help: Use your baseline and expected reduction. Exclude incidents also counted as risk reduction.

incident_cost.label: Incremental cost per error
incident_cost.help: Exclude labor, refunds or other losses already included elsewhere.

probability_before.label: Monthly loss probability before
probability_before.help: Your estimate, not a guaranteed risk assessment.

probability_after.label: Monthly loss probability after
probability_after.help: Use the same event and monthly time horizon as the baseline.

loss.label: Loss exposure for that event
loss.help: Exclude error incidents and spending already counted. This is uncertain expected value, not cash saved.

days_before.label: Cycle time before, in days
days_before.help: Elapsed time from start to completion, separate from hands-on effort.

days_after.label: Cycle time after, in days
days_after.help: Shown as an operational change only, without an assumed euro value.

outcomes.label: Do higher-value work
outcomes.help: Use part of the capacity for work with incremental contribution.

outcomes.label: Handle more volume
outcomes.help: Match available capacity with actual expected demand.

outcomes.label: Stop actual spending
outcomes.help: Reduce overtime, contractors or paid processing—not unchanged salaries.

outcomes.label: Defer a planned hire
outcomes.help: Cover a specific, genuinely planned workload for a stated period.

outcomes.label: Finish sooner
outcomes.help: Show elapsed days improved without automatically attaching a euro value.

cta.privacyNote: Your data stays private. Hours are capacity. Euros are classified modeled value, not observed results.
